newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks stagger in worst week ever for Dow.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks stagger in worst week ever for Dow.

text.p: The stock market tumbled to its second biggest point loss ever Friday as an earnings warning by consumer products giant Gillette Co sparked worries about Corporate America's future profits and another drop in the dollar sparked a major sell-off.
The Dow Jones industrial average sank 247 points to close unofficially at 7695, with the selling knocking more than three percent off the blue chip average.
It was the worst week ever for the Dow, with losses racking up to more than 330 points.

With Friday's loss, the Dow has fallen 6.8 percent from its all-time closing high of 8259.31, set on August 6. Several analysts said the downturn, the first sustained market decline since the nearly 10 percent correction that ended in mid- April, did not yet appear to be at its end.
"We are in a correction from the 8,300 level and we need to test a little further on the downside," said James Volk head of institutional equity trading at Arcadia Investment Corp.

Troubles started at the opening bell, with the Dow falling more than 100 points in the first few minutes of trading. Traders were rattled after Gillette Co told Wall Street it expects disappointing 1997 earnings. On the heels of a similar warnings from Coca-Cola Co last week, this sparked considerable worry about Corporate America's future profits.
Adding to the volatility, it was a double-witching Friday on Wall Street, when many stock futures and index expire.
Volk believed the downturn was not the signal of the beginning of a bear market. But other traders said they had noticed a distinct shift in the mood on Wall Street.

"We're witnessing a transition from buy on weakness to sell on strength...And it wouldn't surprise me if what we're seeing is the footsteps of some program trading," Charlie Crane, chief market strategist at Key Asset Management added.

He said the raging bullishness that was the hallmark of July's stock market no longer had the two-pronged support of lower long-term interest rates and a continual stream of strong corporate earnings, with earnings season about over.
Analysts also noted the drop was exaggerated because many traders were not at work on a summer Friday afternoon, so fewer buyers were around to step in on the weakness.

Consumer products stocks took it on the chin after Gillette's warning. Gillette slumped 4-5/16 to close at 85-7/8 and Procter & Gamble Co lost 7-1/2 to 136-9/16. Colgate-Palmolive Co fell 4-15/16 to 65-1/4.
Drug stocks, banking stocks and multinationals also fell sharply with the dollar, which was depressed amid growing speculationt Germany's central bank might raise interest rates.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 24.66 to 1562.03.
The Standard & Poor's 500 Index erased nearly 24 points, falling 2.6 percent to 900.81.

The long bond managed to remain unchanged despite the weakness in equities, with the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond yielding 6.55 percent. Most analysts say the Federal Reserve will leave interest rates unchanged when its monetary policy committee meets on Tuesday.
Some stocks managed to buck the trend.
Biotechnology company Geron Corp more than doubled after the company said it has successfully cloned a gene that could fight cancer and old age. Shares closed up 7-1/2 to 14.
TV Azteca SA, Mexico's second largest television broadcaster, rose 15/16 to 19-3/16 in heavy trading after its initial public offering.
Another IPO, SL Green Realty Corp, jumped almost 20 percent, rising four to 25 after its market debut. The firm renovates old office buildings in Manhattan.
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1881))
